tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters...'), focuses on the operator's investigative goals (proving log coverage, giving node verdicts, pre-flight readiness) rather than internal implementation, and ends with an explicit, pushy list of trigger contexts ('Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness... or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run"'). It is a dense paragraph but stays within a reasonable length for the breadth of scenarios covered.
tests.evidence: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. ... Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific, non-obvious facts (e.g., instance ID survives reboot but not replace, Capacity Block termination timing, percent-of-percent metric gotchas) rather than explaining general concepts. It avoids restating things the agent already knows.
tests.evidence: R3. 'A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace gives the node a new instance ID in the same instance group...'
